name: Base Power
description: Base Power is privately held and has no ticker. Review its funding rounds and valuations, the investors and SPVs that hold its shares, and the points to confirm before buying or selling.
ledes: Base Power is a privately held energy company. Its shares are not listed on an exchange and have no quoted market price; the principal public reference points are the valuations at which the company has raised capital. Its most recent financing, a $1 billion Series D round announced on August 3, 2026, valued the company at $13 billion.

Founded in 2023 and based in Austin, Texas, Base Power installs large batteries at customers' homes, sells those households electricity and operates the batteries together as a resource for the power grid. Existing shares change hands in privately negotiated transactions, frequently through special purpose vehicles, and remain subject to the company's transfer restrictions.
figs: Special purpose vehicles with SEC filings naming Base Power
table_note: Valuations are post-money. The Series C valuation is as reported by Fortune.
round_notes: In announcing the Series D, Base Power said its fleet of installed batteries exceeded 500 megawatt-hours of storage; that figure is the company's own.

A round valuation reflects the terms of the preferred stock issued in that round. Most shares sold by employees are common stock, which carries fewer rights and typically trades at a discount to the preferred price.
investors: Ribbit, Addition, Valor Equity Partners and JPMorganChase's Strategic Investment Group co-led the Series D. Addition led the Series C, and the Series B was co-led by Andreessen Horowitz, Addition, Valor Equity Partners and Lightspeed Venture Partners. Other investors include Thrive Capital, Altimeter, CapitalG, Coatue, D1 Capital Partners and Sands Capital.
spv_sentence: Since 2023, three special purpose vehicles formed to invest in Base Power have filed with the SEC, one of them in 2026.
sources: Sources: TechCrunch reports dated August 3, 2026, October 8, 2025 and April 9, 2025; reports by Fortune (August 2026) and Bloomberg (October 2025); and SEC Form D filings.
